commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks are listed in the order that they were added, but there is
nothing that can reorder them. Even though deadline/event tasks
already store dates as real dates, the user cannot figure out
what task is due next, and which task is more urgent.

Adding a sort command allows the user to determine which tasks are
more urgent, and also allows the user to sort the task list via
other attributes such as task type and name, allowing the user to
find their desired tasks more quickly instead of having to scroll
through the whole list.

Let's,
* add a sort command taking a key and an optional direction, e.g.
  "sort date" or "sort name desc"
* support four keys: date, name, type and done, where a deadline sorts
  by when it is due and an event sorts by when the event starts
* rearrange the stored tasks and save the new sorted list to the
  device, rather than merely show a sorted view of a list without
  the original list changing.

The original task list is overwritten because the "delete" command
deletes tasks based on the task's numbering, and sorting the list
can caused the task's numberings to change, causing a mismatch between
the original task list and the sorted view of the task list, if the
original task list is not overwritten.

When sorting by date, a todo task with no deadline sorts after every
deadline/event task in both directions, because a todo task is
usually less urgent (i.e. no timeline) compared to deadline/event
tasks. The user can currently list the todo tasks at the front
(before deadline/event tasks) by using the command "sort type".

Tasks that tie after being sorted according to the key, are left in
the order they were previously already in, rather than
separated by a second key.

The save file format is also unchanged after sorting. The same
fields, same separator and same ISO dates are used, in order to
ensure that a file written by an earlier version still loads.
The only difference after sorting comes in which task/line
appears first.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle more command, file and data errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Several mistakes a user can make, and several problems a save file
can have, were accepted without a word, reported in a way that
pointed at the wrong mistake, or could lose tasks.

Let's handle each of them.

Command format errors

1. A separator given twice
   Before: "deadline x /by 2019-10-15 1800 /by 2019-10-16 1800" was
   cut at the first /by, so the date became "2019-10-15 1800 /by
   2019-10-16 1800" and was refused as unreadable. That was true,
   but it pointed at the date rather than at the repeated /by, so
   the user could not tell what to fix.
   Now: a /by, /from or /to that appears again after the first copy
   is refused by name: "Please give the /by part only once." A copy
   before the separator, such as a /to ahead of /from, is still
   ordinary description text.

2. Tabs and other control characters
   Before: "todo<tab>read book" was refused as an unknown command
   with no visible reason, since a tab looks like a space. A tab, or
   the escape code some consoles type for an arrow key, inside a
   description was stored and printed back as garbage.
   Now: a line holding any control character is refused before
   anything else is read, with a message saying so.

3. Task numbers that are not plain digits
   Before: Integer.parseInt accepts a sign and digits from other
   writing systems, so "mark +1" quietly marked task 1 and "mark -1"
   was treated as a task number. Neither is how list shows a number.
   Now: only the digits 0 to 9 are accepted. "+1", "-1" and other
   digits get the "Please give me a task number" hint, while
   "mark 01" still marks task 1.

4. Extra spaces inside a date
   Before: every date layout has exactly one space between the day
   and the time, so "2019-10-15  1800", with two spaces, was refused
   as an unreadable date.
   Now: a run of spaces is read as one before the date is parsed. A
   date that still cannot be read is quoted back exactly as typed.

Data errors

5. An event that ends before, or when, it starts
   Before: "event x /from 2019-10-02 1600 /to 2019-10-02 1400" was
   stored, giving a task that could never take place.
   Now: the Event constructor refuses it and shows both times as the
   bot read them. Loading uses the same constructor, so such a line
   in the save file is skipped as damaged.

6. Duplicate tasks
   Before: the same task could be added any number of times, usually
   by typing it twice. The user was then left with two copies to
   mark and delete, and could finish one while the other stayed
   undone.
   Now: TaskList.add refuses a task with the same kind, description
   and dates as a stored one, ignoring capitals and whether the
   stored one is done, and shows the stored copy with its number.
   Repeats already in the save file are still loaded, so none of the
   user's data is dropped without a word.

7. Marking a task that already has that status
   Before: "mark" on a done task, or "unmark" on one not done,
   confirmed a change that never happened and saved the list again.
   Now: it is refused with the task shown, which also makes a
   mistyped number easy to spot, and nothing is saved.
   Task.isDone() is now public so that MarkCommand can ask.

Save file errors

8. A save that fails part-way
   Before: the save file was written over directly, which empties it
   the moment writing begins, so a full disk or a crash during a
   save could lose every task.
   Now: the tasks are written to piplupbot.txt.tmp first and then
   moved into place in one atomic step. A failed save deletes the
   temporary file and leaves the old save file whole.

9. A second damaged save file
   Before: every damaged start copied the file to the one name
   piplupbot.txt.damaged, so a later damaged start overwrote the
   earlier copy, which could be the only record of the lost tasks.
   Now: a copy with different contents is never replaced; the new
   copy goes to piplupbot.txt.damaged-2, then -3, and so on. A copy
   with identical contents is reused rather than duplicated.

10. A byte order mark at the start of the file
    Before: some editors start a UTF-8 file with an invisible byte
    order mark. It stuck to the first task's type code, so that
    task was skipped as damaged.
    Now: the mark is dropped before the file is split into lines.

11. Blank lines in the save file
    Before: each blank line was counted as a damaged line, giving a
    false warning and a pointless rescue copy.
    Now: blank lines are skipped without a warning, since they hold
    no task.

JUnit tests cover every change: 231 tests, 34 of them new, including
a new MarkCommandTest. The gitignored text-UI test plan gains TC-54
to TC-58 and revises TC-17, TC-20, TC-21, TC-27 and TC-31.

Commit Message Co-Authored-By Claude

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for nearly all non-GUI code
commitResults.messageBody:
Some failure paths (e.g. a save that fails, a rescue copy that cannot be
made, a save file that is not UTF-8) were not tested at all,
although those are the paths where tasks can be lost.

Let's test nearly everything that can run without a window.

New test classes

- UiTest and TextUiTest: how a reply and a list are laid out, the
  banner before the greeting, trimmed input, and input running out.
- AddCommandTest, DeleteCommandTest, FindCommandTest, ListCommandTest
  and SortCommandTest: each command's exact reply, whether it saves
  the list, and that a refused command says and saves nothing.
- PiplupBotExceptionTest: getMessage() joins the lines with spaces.
- GuiUiTest: getResourceUrl(), the one GUI method that needs no window.

Cases added to existing classes

- PiplupBotTest: greet() with a clean and with a damaged save file, and
  run() stopping at bye and when the input runs out.
- CommandTest: a failed save is reported rather than thrown, and a new
  command does not end the conversation.
- StorageTest: the wording of a failed save, a file that is not UTF-8,
  a rescue copy that cannot be made, the name of a third copy, reusing
  the second copy, a temporary folder that cannot be removed, and a
  lone backslash at the end of a field.
- ParserTest, TodoTest and SortKeyTest: two hint messages, several
  spaces before a sort direction, and a Turkish default locale.

A shared test helper

RecordingUi, a Ui that keeps its replies instead of showing them, was
nested inside PiplupBotTest and MarkCommandTest. It now has a file of
its own under src/test, so the nine test classes that need it share
one copy instead of each keeping its own.

What is still checked by hand

GuiUi (apart from getResourceUrl), DialogBox and Launcher need a
running JavaFX window, which a build machine does not have, so they
stay manual checks. Every new test that guards a decision was checked
by undoing that decision in src/main: all 32 such changes made the
intended test fail.

Co-Authored-By: Claude

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate respondTo into a command & an isExit query
commitResults.messageBody: respondTo both carried out a line and returned whether it ended the conversation, so its name could not describe both jobs. It now returns void, and the new isExit() answers the question from a field that respondTo sets. run() and GuiUi ask isExit() after each line instead of reading a return value

commitResults.messageTitle: Rephrase header comments to follow coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Class, enum and interface headers that opened with a noun phrase ("A task that ...", "The words PiplupBot recognises ...") now open with a third-person verb: usually "Represents ...", or "Handles ..." for the static helper DateTimes and "Starts ..." for Launcher. Methods and test helpers that return a value now open with "Returns ..." in place of Builds/Renders/Turns/Lists/Joins/Reads.

@param/@return/@throws descriptions are now capitalised sentences ending in a full stop, as in the standard's Javadoc example. British spellings in Javadoc comments are now American.

Also corrects comments that had drifted from the code: load() listed three failure cases but said four; the command hint example left out sort; the numbered-line example used the wrong date format; and Deadline still called sorting a future feature.

Test-case comments that state the rule being checked are left as they are: the standard does not require headers on test methods, and these explain why each case exists.

Co-Authored by: Claude

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename identifiers to follow SE-EDU naming rules
commitResults.messageBody:
The SE-EDU Java coding standard requires method names to be verbs,
collections to have plural names, and associated constants to share a
common prefix. A review of src/main and src/test found names breaking
each of these rules.

Methods now start with a verb: strictPattern, argumentOf and
withExtraFields become createStrictFormatter, extractArgument and
buildFileFields. The test helpers follow suit, e.g. saveFile becomes
getSaveFile, as it only returns a path but read like an action. The
argumentOf_ test names change with the method they test.

Collections in the tests are plural: warning becomes warningLines, and
original, list, ordered, copy and seen gain a plural noun.

Associated constants share a prefix, so each group sorts and
autocompletes together: INDEX_* in Storage, SEPARATOR_* in Parser and
IMAGE_PATH_* in GuiUi.

Three misleading names are also fixed: displayPath formats rather than
displays (now formatPath), separator in splitIntoParts held a position
(now separatorIndex), and reversed in SortCommand held text rather than
a flag (now reversedNote).

Deadline.by and Event.from/to keep their names, matching the /by, /from
and /to the user types.

Behaviour is unchanged: all 58 text-UI test cases and 272 JUnit tests
pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude
